title: WPMB/223/2025 of M/S LAKSHAY CONSTRUCTIONS Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
2026:UHC:3298-DB
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA
AND
HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE SUBHASH UPADHYAY
30TH APRIL, 2026
WRIT PETITION (M/B) NO. 223 OF 2025
M/s Lakshay Constructions ......Petitioner.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others ....Respondents.
Counsel for the Petitioner : Mr. Rajendra Singh Azad, learned
counsel through video conferencing.
Counsel for Respondent No.1 : Mr. Yogesh Chandra Tiwari, learned
Standing Counsel.
Counsel for Respondent Nos.2 to 4 : Mr. S.S. Chauhan, learned counsel.
JUDGMENT :(per Mr. Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)
1. The petitioner- firm, feeling aggrieved by order
dated 01.05.2025, passed by respondent- Department
cancelling the tender process आई0Mh0
2025_MDPEY_81464_1, has filed the present writ petition.
2. The reason given for cancelling the tender
process is that the bid of the petitioner- firm, though L1, is
still on a much higher side than the bids received in respect
of the same work in the previous round of the tender
process. Thus, the respondent- Department has decided to
invite fresh bids.
3. The case of the petitioner- firm is that after its
has made the bid, the Department vide letter dated
23.04.2025 required the petitioner to lower its bid and in
1

2026:UHC:3298-DB
response to the same, the petitioner-firm further reduced
its bid amount by 1%, but still the respondents have
cancelled the bidding process, which is illegal. It is urged
that the petitioner-firm should be given further opportunity
to lower its bid.
4. The respondent- Department has filed counter-affidavit and the stand taken is that in the past also,
tenders were invited in respect of the same work. In the
said tender process one M/s Naseem Ahmad was L1 and its
bid was for Rs.87,19,638.20/-, i.e. 21.77% below the
departmental rates. The petitioner- firm was L2 bidder and
its bid was for Rs.93,77,022.89/-, i.e. 15.52% below the
departmental rates, however, on its complaint, the bid of
M/s Naseem Ahmad, L1 bidder was cancelled. Thereafter, in
the present tender process, though the bid of the
petitioner-firm is L1, but the amount quoted by it is
Rs.1,10,03,373.98/-, i.e. only 0.87% below the rates
quoted by the Department and even after reduction by 1%,
it is much above the bid quoted by the petitioner-firm in the
previous tender process.
5. The Tender Committee of the respondent-Department, after considering all the relevant aspects and
in the interest of revenue, decided to cancel the tender
process and invite fresh tenders. The bid given by the
2

2026:UHC:3298-DB
petitioner-firm was merely an offer made by it. The
Department, keeping in view its financial interest, has
decided to go for fresh tenders. Undisputedly, the bid for
the same work made by the petitioner- firm in the previous
tender process was much lower. In such circumstances, it
cannot be said that the decision of the Tender Committee
suffers from any manifest illegality to warrant interference
under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
6. Consequently, the writ petition is dismissed.
7. Pending application, if any, also stands disposed
of.
MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA, C.J.
SUBHASH UPADHYAY, J.
Dated: 30th April, 2026
NISHANT
